So, I filled to 32 ounce glasses, dumped them and tried the water. The taste is excellent, that is, no taste other than water. That's what I am after. Job well done!

This is a scam as several other reviewers noticed. First, the "Blue Signature" water filter claims a NSF testing for both NSF 42 & 53. Looking up the NSF database shows no product certification for "Blue Signature". You can check it on the info-nfs-org website.

In addition, the brand "Blue Signature" claims to be trademarked "TM" but it is not. A trademark search only shows Colgate-Palmolive as a registrant for a personal care product by the name "Blue Signature". You can check it on the USPTO-TESS database.
Product was as advertised.  Good price, quick delivery.  I would definitely recommend this company.

I wanted to like this product because the customer service was very good replacing the first filter I bought that did not provide me with clean tasting water. The customer service person thought it was due to a defective unit and sent a replacement. But, unfortunately the replacement provided the same result. When first installed the filter didn't do too badly. The water didn't taste as good as the two other filters we have used from other companies but it wasn't too bad. But, after about a week I started to notice a plastic taste to the water as as more time went on the taste got worse. After two tries with this company's filter I returned it for a refund and went back to the GE brand that we have had good experience with. After putting in the new GE filter I could notice a big difference in the taste of the water right away. So, we will stick with the GE filter even though these folks have been very nice.

Not NSF 53 certified. Manufacture can use whatever marketing spin they want, but if its not NSF 53 certified, the use of that term anywhere in its product description implying that is it should be taken out.

Not made in the use. As per the FTC, the use of the American flag implies that the product is made in the USA and violates their "Made in the USA" standard.

Shameful business practice that should not go rewarded with your money.

And then do a final hard press without twisting...just blow the extra coffee grinds away before removing tamper. Not hard to figure out if you're tamping okay...just look at the puck after you remove it (is it still solid or are there little valleys and uneveness...you want it solid).

I don't drink espresso daily, nor am I an expert with the machine, frothing, tamping, etc. So...paying a reasonable price made more sense to me. I'd rather spend more on organic fairly traded beans.

My last three coffee beans have been from Amazon...I like Jo Espresso, The Organic Coffee Company Rainforest blend. Using basic Krups $20 grinder...also purchased from Amazon many years ago.

If, however, you care a little for our world, as we all urgently need to, then you need to use these things if you use a Keurig. The little things count. The good:
* Good price and corresponding value given what's included
* Single cup variety works great with older generation Keurig brewers
* Amazon delivery speed and convenience

The bad:
* Unfortunately I have had issues with these on our new Keurig 2.0 (575 model in our case) brewing fairly weak coffee. When I say weak, I mean severely so rather than just a matter of preference. In order to isolate the problem I tested these Luxe reusable filters with a Keurig branded disposable variety and it was night and day. Bear in mind that I tried multiple types of coffee grounds in the reusable including fine, medium and coarse. The watered down / weak coffee was the worst using the carafe larger filter
POSSIBLE SOLUTION: After some disappointed Googling around to find an answer, the only one I could find that seemed to help was to pack down the coffee grounds in the reusable filter prior to brewing and that definitely helped. This is less ideal though because (a) its an extra step beyond simply pouring the grounds into the filter and (b) it means one more thing to clean up. For these reasons I rated the product a 3-star ("its OK")

I think the main issue seems to be the speed at which the hot water passes through the coffee grounds (thus why packing in the grounds seems to help, it basically slows down the water flow). It seems the design should be improved to somehow channel or restrict the water flow. Maybe less mesh f

These Reusable K-Karafe K-Cup Pods work very well when you want to use your own coffee and wish to save money as well!  I have used both the large purple one with my K-Carafe and the smaller orange ones when making just a single mug of coffee.  They save money and are great to have if you run out of the regular pods and keep ground coffee or coffee beans on hand.  I was a little concerned when I purchased them that they may not work properly with my new Keurig 2.0 coffeemaker because Keurig now has made this coffeemaker so it only accepts pre-filled pods that have Keurig on them...generic pods do not work with this model.  It is something to think about when purchasing a new Keurig and something I did not know before I purchased it!  (My new one is my third Keurig coffeemaker.)
